title: The enemy called desire
hookLine: Arjuna asks why people do what they know is wrong, as if pushed by force, and Krishna names the enemy
carry: desire and anger: the enemy that hides the self
last: LOKASANGRAHA — WHAT THE BEST DO, OTHERS FOLLOW.

cards: Ten minutes after the text someone swore they wouldn't send, a small question shows up: why did I do that? I knew better.

The same question follows the third helping, the thing said in anger, the app opened again at midnight. As if something else had its hands on the wheel. Near the end of chapter three, Arjuna asks exactly this.
What pushes a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against their own will, as if forced? Krishna's answer is short, and it names two things.

teach.b: First Krishna gathers up the chapter: offer all your actions to me, and fight, free of fever. Then verse thirty-five. Shreyan svadharmo vigunah, paradharmat svanushthitat.

Better your own dharma, done imperfectly, than someone else's done well. Someone else's path, however well walked, is full of fear. Then Arjuna's question: atha kena prayukto 'yam papam charati purushah.

teach.h: WHAT DRIVES US, AS IF FORCED?
teach.b: By what is a person driven to do wrong, even unwillingly, as if forced? Krishna's answer: kama esha krodha esha. It is desire.
It is anger. Born of restlessness, the quality called rajas, all-devouring, the great wrong. Know this, he says, as the enemy.
Then three pictures of how it hides. As fire is covered by smoke. As a mirror is covered by dust.
As a baby is covered by the womb. The light is still there; you just can't see it.

This enemy is like a fire that's never satisfied, and it lives in the senses, the mind and the understanding, using them to cloud what you know. So Krishna gives an order of strength. The senses are powerful.

The mind is higher than the senses, the understanding higher than the mind, and higher than understanding is the self. Steady yourself by the self, and then: jahi shatrum mahabaho kamarupam durasadam.
Strike down, mighty-armed one, this enemy in the form of desire, so hard to overcome.

teach.h: STRIKE DOWN THE ENEMY CALLED DESIRE.
teach.b: The action was never the problem. The grasping is.

how: Gita 3.35, better one's own dharma imperfectly than another's well, and 3.37, naming desire and anger as the enemy, are verses some Hindus learn by heart and return to when facing a hard choice.

o: fate, pushing us as if forced

games.q: what's inside the enemy — tap the pairs.

s: the Gita says it's better to do another's path well than your own badly
better your own dharma, done imperfectly, than another's done well.
Krishna names desire and anger as the enemy
kama esha krodha esha: it is desire, it is anger, born of rajas.
the Gita says the self is higher than the understanding
senses, then mind, then understanding, and higher than understanding, the self.

games.q: you're Arjuna. you've noticed people do wrong even when they don't want to, as if forced. what do you do?
games.why: he asks: by what is a person driven to do wrong, even unwillingly? Krishna answers: desire and anger. know this as the enemy.

practice: Picture a mirror under a fine layer of dust: that's how a strong want sits over what you already know.
Think of one thing you do even though you know better, and name the want underneath it plainly, I want comfort, I want to be right, I want more, without fighting it.
With each out-breath, picture one slow wipe across the glass; behind the dust, the mirror was always clear.

wordCard.voice: Kama. Desire, named with anger as the enemy. What drives us to act against what we know, hiding like smoke over fire, dust over a mirror.
